seo.title: Halette: Greek Goddess of Fertility and Childbirth in Christianity
seo.meta_description: Discover the meaning, origins, and religious significance of the Greek goddess Halette, the goddess of fertility and childbirth in Christianity.
seo.description_paragraph:
Halette, also known as Haleia or Hera, is a Greek goddess of fertility and childbirth. Her name comes from the Greek word halos, meaning 'salt' or 'wavy.' She is often depicted as a woman with a cornucopia, overflowing with fruits and vegetables.

In Greek mythology, Halette is one of the twelve Olympian gods and goddesses. She is the sister and wife of Zeus, the king of the gods. She is also the protector of women and children, and is invoked to help ensure a safe and healthy pregnancy and childbirth. Her cult was particularly popular among women and midwives.

Halette's religious significance in Christianity is less clear, but she is sometimes identified with the Virgin Mary, who is also associated with fertility and childbirth. Some sources suggest that Halette's cult may have been absorbed into Christianity, and that her feast day was celebrated on September 8, the same day as the feast of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
